name: Graphite violet
lede: Graphite violet is a mid-grey with a faint violet lean, one of ColorHub's own core names built as a violet-leaning variant of graphite.

sections.title: A mineral-word family variant
sections.body:
This name is built on the mineral word graphite, placed in our naming system as a violet-leaning variant of the family rather than copied from a single dated source [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system would file its neutral, slightly purplish character in the dark purplish gray range, at Munsell N 4.0 [1]. Which historical plate or dictionary, if any, used this exact name is undocumented in the sources checked here [1].

It reads lighter than the library's own Graphite, a 1915 Maerz and Paul entry at a much darker value, and a different hue from the grey-toned, RAL-sourced Graphite Grey [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[plumbago-slate]], [[blackish-grey]] and [[smoke]], at 2.6, 
Its family parent, [[graphite]], and the neutral [[slate]] both sit nearby in ColorHub's own color map [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this grey in 378 of 23,781 paintings, about one and a half per cent [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 31 of 1,674 paintings, at roughly three times the overall baseline rate [2]. The earliest match is a 1119 Buddhist manuscript page, eight centuries before this name entered ColorHub's own naming system, so that is a lookalike hue, not a pigment record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings and manuscripts, and a match is a computed color comparison, not a material identification [2].
